scenes.headline: How a 744B model runs on a 25 GB machine
scenes.sub: Colibri keeps the dense core in RAM and streams experts from disk.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cinnamon! Colibri runs GLM-5.2, a seven hundred forty-four billion parameter model, on a machine with twenty-five gigabytes of RAM. Here's how.

scenes.text: Keep what every token touches resident in RAM. Leave the rarely used experts on disk, and stream them in on demand.
scenes.say: The idea: keep what every token touches in RAM. Leave the rarely used experts on disk, and stream them in on demand.

steps.label: 256 experts in each MoE layer
steps.say: GLM-5.2 is a mixture of experts. Each of its MoE layers holds two hundred fifty-six of them.

steps.label: About 40B of 744B active per token
steps.say: But a router picks only a few per token. About forty billion parameters are active, and only the routed experts change between tokens.
Attention, shared experts and embeddings run on every token. That dense core stays in RAM, quantized to int4: nine point nine gigabytes.
When the router picks its experts, check a RAM cache of hot ones first.
A hit is served at memory speed.
A miss reads about nineteen megabytes from disk, on the critical path. The token can't finish until the bytes arrive.

items.say: A cache sized from free memory keeps repeat experts hot.
Reading ahead fetches the next experts while the current ones multiply.
Pinning keeps your most-used experts resident, so it gets faster the more you use it.

items.text: Draft tokens with MTP at int8
items.say: And the model's own draft head proposes tokens at int8. Once the cache is warm, one pass yields more than two.

scenes.title: Decode speed, tokens per second
scenes.note: community-reported single runs; every rung is bought with memory
scenes.say: Cold, it's ten to twenty seconds a token: the disk sets the pace. Every rung up the ladder is bought with more memory.

scenes.text: A sparse model's active footprint, not its parameter count, is what has to sit in fast memory.
scenes.say: A sparse model's active footprint, not its parameter count, is what has to sit in fast memory.

recap: The int4 dense core lives in RAM
Routed experts stream from about 370 GB of disk
Caching, pinning and MTP push back on the disk
scenes.say: To recap: the core lives in RAM, experts stream from disk, and caching and drafting push back on the wait.
